nodes.content: Build an incremental Java taint analyzer preserving interprocedural soundness when edits change heap aliasing and virtual dispatch.
requirements: For Java without reflection or native calls, findings must equal sound, context-sensitive whole-program recomputation.
Achieve ≥3× median speedup over full recomputation on a fixed suite of 100 method-body edits.

nodes.content: Maintain provenance-indexed, context-sensitive heap points-to, virtual-call targets, and taint facts; retract and recompute affected dependency SCCs.
How can newly introduced aliases and virtual targets trigger complete taint updates without recomputing unaffected contexts?
Provenance-indexed alias and dispatch edges with affected-SCC closure should match recomputed findings while revisiting under 40% of facts.
Track provenance-backed alias and dispatch deltas, recompute transitive dependent context-sensitive SCCs, validate findings and speedup on 100 edits.
Run AliasDispatch-100 method-body edits against context-sensitive whole-program recomputation, measuring finding equality, median speedup, and revisited-fact fraction.
On AliasDispatch-100, all 100 edits matched whole-program findings; median speedup was 3.7×, with 28% of facts revisited.
Adopt provenance-indexed affected-SCC recomputation as the implementation baseline; AliasDispatch-100 met finding equality and the 3× speedup target.
Implement the adopted affected-SCC engine with provenance invalidation for heap-store deletions and virtual-target changes, plus AliasDispatch-100 regression gates.
IncrementalTaintEngine.java and AliasDispatch-100 tests implement provenance-backed alias/dispatch invalidation and gate exact findings and ≥3× median speedup.
Heap-object and receiver-type subscriptions should preserve exact findings on alias-heavy edits while revisiting under 25% of context facts.
Extend IncrementalTaintEngine.java with heap-object and receiver-type subscriptions; benchmark alias-heavy edits against whole-program findings and baseline revisited-fact fraction.
On AliasHeavy-30, subscriptions missed two sink findings after receiver-type widening, despite revisiting only 19% of context facts.
Fall back to whole-program recomputation on receiver widening, repair subscriptions, then rerun AliasHeavy-30 and AliasDispatch-100 correctness and speedup gates.
Patch IncrementalTaintEngine.java with receiver-widening fallback and new-target subscriptions; rerun AliasHeavy-30 and AliasDispatch-100 against whole-program recomputation.
IncrementalTaintEngine.java now falls back on receiver widening and subscribes to new targets; regression tests cover AliasHeavy-30 and AliasDispatch-100.
Benchmark patched IncrementalTaintEngine.java on AliasHeavy-30 and AliasDispatch-100, comparing findings, affected-SCC coverage, and median speedup against recomputation.
Patched engine matched whole-program findings on all 130 edits; affected-SCC coverage was 100%, with 3.3× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Use differential Datalog with delete/rederive to incrementally maintain context-sensitive points-to, virtual-call, and taint relations from edited method facts.
Can delete/rederive handle cyclic heap aliases and newly reachable virtual targets without stale taint facts or excessive recomputation?
Benchmark differential Datalog against patched IncrementalTaintEngine.java and whole-program recomputation on CyclicAliasDispatch-40, measuring finding parity and median latency.
On CyclicAliasDispatch-40, affected-SCC missed four sink findings after cyclic alias deletions; differential Datalog matched all 40 whole-program outputs.
Differential Datalog delete/rederive should preserve whole-program finding parity under cyclic alias deletions and virtual-target changes.
Implement differential delete/rederive for cyclic aliases and dispatch; verify finding parity on CyclicAliasDispatch-40 and ≥3× speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Integrate differential delete/rederive into IncrementalTaintEngine.java; compare CyclicAliasDispatch-40 findings and AliasDispatch-100 median speedup against whole-program recomputation.
Integrated delete/rederive produced two spurious sink findings on CyclicAliasDispatch-40 because context-memoized virtual targets survived alias-cycle deletion.
Context-keyed overdelete-and-rederive of memoized dispatch targets alongside cyclic points-to facts should eliminate spurious findings without losing parity.
Patch IncrementalTaintEngine.java with context-keyed dispatch overdelete/rederive; check CyclicAliasDispatch-40 finding parity and AliasDispatch-100 median speedup.
On CyclicAliasDispatch-40, context-keyed rederivation removed spurious findings but missed one sink when shared heap taint crossed contexts.
Tracking shared-heap taint dependencies across contexts during dispatch rederivation should restore finding parity on CyclicAliasDispatch-40.
Add cross-context shared-heap taint dependencies to IncrementalTaintEngine.java; rerun CyclicAliasDispatch-40 for finding parity and AliasDispatch-100 for median speedup.
Cross-context heap dependencies restored all 40 CyclicAliasDispatch findings; AliasDispatch-100 median speedup was 3.1× versus recomputation.
Adopt differential delete/rederive with context-keyed dispatch and cross-context heap dependencies; cyclic-edit parity holds while median speedup remains 3.1×.
Harden IncrementalTaintEngine.java’s adopted differential maintenance with seeded alias/dispatch edits and whole-program finding-parity assertions.
IncrementalTaintEngine.java now uses context-keyed dispatch delete/rederive and cross-context heap dependencies; seeded alias/dispatch tests assert whole-program finding parity.
Which differential-rule indexes propagate newly instantiated receiver types into virtual calls and heap taint without scanning every context?
Profile IncrementalTaintEngine.java on DispatchGrowth-50; test receiver-type call and allocation-site/field heap indexes for finding parity and latency.
On DispatchGrowth-50, receiver-type/call and allocation-site/field indexes preserved 50/50 whole-program finding parity, reducing median latency from 92 to 41 ms.
Integrate receiver-type/call and allocation-site/field indexes, then verify parity and ≥3× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Integrate validated receiver-type/call and allocation-site/field indexes into IncrementalTaintEngine.java; rerun AliasDispatch-100 for finding parity and median speedup.
IncrementalTaintEngine.java now indexes virtual calls by receiver type and heap dependencies by allocation-site/field, updating the differential-maintenance implementation.
Benchmark indexed versus unindexed differential maintenance on AliasDispatch-100, checking whole-program finding parity, median speedup, and dispatch/heap-context scans.
On AliasDispatch-100, indexed differential maintenance matched all recomputed findings, scanned 61% fewer contexts, and achieved 3.8× median speedup.
Retain indexed differential maintenance: AliasDispatch-100 achieved exact recomputation parity and 3.8× median speedup while scanning fewer contexts.
Use versioned context-sensitive summaries and demand-driven sink slices, invalidating callers and shared-heap readers on alias or dispatch changes.
How can demand-driven slices discover newly reachable sinks when edits create alias or dispatch edges outside cached slices?
Versioned reachability frontiers at call sites and heap fields should expose newly reachable sinks with exact finding parity.
Prototype versioned call-site and heap-field frontiers atop indexed IncrementalTaintEngine.java; test new-sink recall and finding parity on DispatchGrowth-50.
On DispatchGrowth-50, frontier slicing missed three newly reachable sinks when an edit introduced an unseen receiver allocation site.
Global allocation-site insertion events should refresh type-matched call-site and heap-field frontiers, restoring DispatchGrowth-50 finding parity.
Subscribe indexed demand-driven call-site and heap-field frontiers to allocation-site insertions; compare DispatchGrowth-50 findings and AliasDispatch-100 speedup against recomputation.
Allocation-site subscriptions recovered all 50 DispatchGrowth findings; demand-driven slicing achieved 4.2× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100 with exact finding parity.
Adopt demand-driven slicing only with global allocation-site subscriptions; unsubscribed frontiers missed sinks, while subscribed frontiers achieved parity and 4.2× speedup.
Pair indexed differential Datalog with allocation-site-subscribed sink slices, propagating every edit delta before selectively updating findings.
Can global delta propagation preserve ≥3× median speedup when allocation-site edits activate many virtual targets and sink slices?
Integrate global delta propagation with subscribed slices; benchmark allocation-burst edits and AliasDispatch-100 for finding parity and median speedup.
Benchmark hybrid propagation on AllocationBurst-25 and AliasDispatch-100 against recomputation, recording finding parity, activated slices, and median speedup.
AllocationBurst-25/ AliasDispatch-100 benchmark report records whole-program finding comparisons, activated-slice counts, and median hybrid-versus-recomputation latency.
Analyze benchmark report against indexed IncrementalTaintEngine.java, attributing allocation-burst slice costs and verifying finding parity and 3× speedup.
Hybrid propagation matched recomputed findings but achieved only 2.4× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100; allocation bursts activated 78% of slices.
Can delta-triggered slice activation reduce AllocationBurst-25’s 78% fanout and restore ≥3× median speedup without missing sinks?
Type-and-field-keyed frontier subscriptions should lower activated slices below 35% while preserving exact findings and ≥3× AliasDispatch-100 speedup.
Replace broad allocation-site subscriptions with type-and-field-keyed frontier indexes; rerun AllocationBurst-25 and AliasDispatch-100 for activation, parity, and speedup.
Implement type/field frontier indexes in IncrementalTaintEngine.java; benchmark AllocationBurst-25 and AliasDispatch-100 parity, slice activation, and speedup against baseline report.
Type/field indexing matched recomputed findings on both suites; AllocationBurst-25 activated 29% of slices, and AliasDispatch-100 median speedup reached 3.4×.
Use type/field-keyed frontier subscriptions: broad subscriptions achieved 2.4×, whereas indexed activation preserved parity and reached 3.4×.
